In mathematics, a '''binomial ring''' is a [[commutative ring]] whose additive [[group (mathematics)|group]] is [[torsion (algebra)|torsion-free]] and contains all [[binomial coefficient]]s

:<math>\binom{x}{n} = \frac{x(x-1)\cdots(x-n+1)}{n!}</math>

for ''x'' in the ring and ''n'' a positive integer. Binomial rings were introduced by {{harvtxt|Hall|1969}}.

{{harvtxt|Elliott|2006}} showed that binomial rings are essentially the same as [[lambda ring|&lambda;-rings]] for which all [[Adams operation]]s are the identity.
